title: Annotated Prompt Replay Tape — sketch
content:
Goal:
- Define a compact, append-only "prompt tape" format that clients/proxies can emit to enable deterministic replay, offline diagnostics, and lightweight QA/eval without shipping entire model inputs to backend.

Motivation / constraints:
- Need to support streaming, incremental edits, function/tool call metadata, and partial token-level annotations (confidence, chunking markers).
- Tape must be small (prefers line-delimited events), stable across client versions, and tolerant to lossy transport.
- Should enable: replay into local test harness, reconstruct minimal context for cache warmers, and produce diffs for regression debugging.
- Privacy: tape should allow redaction markers and selective hashing of PII.

High-level model:
- Tape = line-delimited events (ndjson-like). Each event is a simple map encoded as JSON string (one line). Event types are small set: session-start, user-edit, system-insert, stream-token, tool-call, tool-result, session-end, meta.
- Each event MUST include: ts, ev, seq, session_id, source_id (client id), opt tags.
- Optional fields: checksum (sha256 hex of event payload) for tamper detection, redact_mask (list of field paths), hash_fields (list of field paths replaced by keyed-hash), local_nonce.

Example event (single line):
{"ts":"2025-02-11T18:21:03.123Z","ev":"session-start","seq":"1","session_id":"s-0a3f","source_id":"mobile-72","user":"user:alice@example.com","meta":"proto=v2;client=ios-1.5"}

Streaming tokens: we emit token events as small units so replays can be deterministic: 
{"ts":"2025-02-11T18:21:04.045Z","ev":"stream-token","seq":"2","session_id":"s-0a3f","source_id":"mobile-72","role":"assistant","token":"▁Hello","token_index":"0","partial_hash":"e3b0c4..."}

User edits: clients may send edits as diffs referencing last stable seq (use simple operational transform-ish patch):
{"ts":"2025-02-11T18:21:10.987Z","ev":"user-edit","seq":"5","session_id":"s-0a3f","source_id":"mobile-72","base_seq":"3","patch":"replace:content[12..18]=\"NYC\""}

Tool call/structured outputs: capture function-call name, args, and opaque tool-id. Tool results may be large; include reference pointers (s3 presigned or local store id) and optional inline preview.
{"ts":"2025-02-11T18:22:00.111Z","ev":"tool-call","seq":"7","session_id":"s-0a3f","tool":"calendar.lookup","args_preview":"{\"range\":\"next_week\"}","tool_ref":"stash://t-8f7"}

Security / privacy primitives:
- redact_mask: client can mark JSON field paths to redact at ingest (e.g., ["user.email","tool_call.args"]). Redwood backend will observe mask and can enforce additional redaction policies.
- hash_fields: client may provide keyed-hash placeholders for values that must not be stored in plaintext but should match on replay to detect changes.
- consent_token: optional per-session consent artifact to indicate user-approved telemetry.

Replay semantics:
- Replay harness must process events in increasing seq and apply semantics according to event type. Client-side replay examples: reconstruct prompt up to seq N by applying session-start then applying user-edit patches and stream-tokens in order.
- Determinism requirement: tokenization used during replay should match one of recorded tokenizers in meta; mismatch should produce an invariant error but allow fallback 'approx token align' mode.

Use cases:
1) Local dev replay: developer runs a tape through the local model to reproduce an assistant response and validate a candidate model change.
2) Cache prewarmer: lightweight process consumes tapes to feed KV cache warmers (only need token events and sequence map).
3) Regression diffing: run two models against same tape and summarize divergence in assistant tokens and function-calls.
4) Support: attach tape to support ticket (with redact/hashes) so SRE/CS can replay without full PII.

On-disk layout suggestions:
- file-per-session per-day: session-<session_id>-YYYYMMDD.log (append-only).
- chunk rotation: limit 20MB per file, write index lines with earliest/latest seq for fast seeking.

Indexing for quick search:
- Sidecar index file (ldjson) with entries: session_id, first_ts, last_ts, last_seq, tags. Keep small.

Implementation notes / pragmatic choices tried in prototypes:
- Initially tried full 'delta' OT format; too heavy for mobile clients. Settled on lightweight patch strings and base_seq pointer.
- Avoid capturing full assistant model logits; just token text and optional token-level quality score float between 0-1.
- Keep event shape stable (v1) and add 'proto=v2' metadata for future changes; server will accept v1/v2 and normalize to canonical internal representation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Canonical patch language: do we vendor a tiny diff DSL or accept a minimal JSON Patch subset? (tradeoffs: readability vs size vs complexity)
- Best hashing scheme for cross-client verification without revealing PII (HKDF + per-customer salt?).
- How to support multi-device session joins where two devices emit overlapping seq ranges? (merge heuristics needed).
- Retention policy and opt-out UX: where to present to user and how to delete a tape.

Quick ASCII diagram (event flow):
client -> (tape write) -> local store (append) -> optional upload -> redwood-ingest -> indexer -> storage
                             |                                   ^
                             -> local-replay-runner ----------------

Small replay example (toy):
- events: session-start(seq1), user-edit(seq2), stream-token(seq3 token=Hi), stream-token(seq4 token=there), tool-call(seq5), tool-result(seq6)
- replay: apply session-start -> apply edit -> assemble tokens [Hi there] -> call tool handler -> attach tool result -> final assistant output = tokens + structured call

Backwards compatibility note:
- If client sends unknown event type, server MUST persist the event (opaque) and index basic fields (ts,seq,session_id) so downstream tools can handle new types without loss.

Appendix: small lint rules for tapes emitted by Redwood clients:
- max line length 64k (reject/rotate if exceed), UTF-8 normalized (NFC), timestamps in ISO-8601 UTC with ms precision, seq is monotonically increasing per session and gaps are allowed (gaps mean missing events rather than reorder).

Action items (next steps):
- Prototype ingest adapter in serving-runtime to accept 1k tapes/day and produce index + sanitized copy. (owner: Marcus)
- Draft client SDK helpers for iOS/Android (owner: Leah)
- Design retention + UI in Console for uploaded tapes (product sync).

Notes to self: keep this format intentionally permissive at first; aim for good defaults and make stricter rules after 3 months of live telemetry.
